Plain seasonal common sense with no figure, date, rule, program or quote, so no outside source is needed. Source line is the general-knowledge line. Rows are four true uses of chopped leaves: mulch around trees, shrubs and beds; a blanket on the roots in the cold; a compost pile; they feed the soil as they break down. The thick-pile line in Titan's sentence is the reason to mow, not a use.
headline:
Fallen Leaves Make Free Mulch
Mow Them, Don't Bag Them
titan_line: Echo, if you don't want to rake, just run the mower over the leaves. Chopped leaves are useful, and a thick pile can smother the lawn.
rows: Mulch: spread chopped leaves around trees, shrubs and flower beds.
In the cold they work like a blanket on the roots.
Compost: chopped leaves are a good addition to a compost pile.
Soil: as they break down, chopped leaves feed the soil.
echo_line: Mulch, compost and richer soil. Those leaves work harder than I do.
disclaimer: General home information. Check your own yard and mower before you start.
